Trying to wrap up Octopath Traveler on the Switch. Also started playing Halo CE again on PC. With some tweaks and mods the game still holds up really well. It's just as fun as it was 15 years ago. Several hundred people still playing the game online too.
How long did Octopath take to beat? Good impressions or lackluster?

I haven't finished the game yet, but I reckon it'll take me 100 hours (currently around 90+). I tried doing a bunch of stuff without walkthroughs as much as possible, so the total play time can definitely be reduced if you know what you're doing.

Overall though, it's mostly ok. The pacing is completely borked thanks to the recommended levels to tackle character specific chapters. Recommended levels for chapter 1 is in the low levels, low-mid 20s for chapter 2, low to mid 30s for chapter 3, and low to mid 40s for chapter 4. This means that if you want to complete the story of one character, you better prepare to get wrecked unless you grind. With the way the game is set up, you are essentially forced to play 1 chapter per character, i.e. clear all eight first chapters, then chapter 2, and so on.

Also, due to there being eight characters, the character stories aren't that good. They feel more like side quests, especially since some of the characters' reasons for setting out just weren't interesting. The endings aren't much better either. Supposedly the epilogue ties all the stories of the characters up, but I'll make up my mind about how good that is once I get to it. On top of all this, there is absolutely no dialogue between any of the characters during cutscenes. The only time you'll see them talking to each other is during banter during certain parts of the stories, and even then they're optional. For the bulk of the game, it feels like you're just playing as one character, with the other 3 only really helping you in battle.

As for the gameplay itself, it's nothing special really. There's been plenty of RPGs in the past where you can combine character classes (or jobs in this game). Other games did it better too. The dungeons aren't anything to write home about either. There's really no puzzle solving or anything, you just trudge on through small-ish dungeons until you get to the boss, defeat it, move on. There's some hidden treasure boxes in these dungeons where you have to look hard for the paths to access them, but that's about it. The character abilities outside of battle make things slightly more interesting. Many side quests will make use of these abilities too.

Speaking of side quests, as if the main game wasn't dialogue heavy already, practically all the NPCs will pretty much give you their life stories when you return to them to complete the quest. JUST STFU AND GIVE ME MY REWARD ALREADY. Thankfully you can skip these cutscenes entirely by holding down the B button.

What is great though are the unique visuals and the soundtrack. If it weren't for those I think I'd have sold the game already.

TL;DR Octopath Traveler was a disappointment IMO, skip this unless you really love JRPGs and have nothing else to play in this genre.
